title: The break cue point
hook: 1 cue point that makes 90s rap mix cleaner.
voiceover: 1 cue point that makes 90s rap mix cleaner. Most 90s rap records were built on a drum loop. Before the first verse, or between verses, there's usually a stretch where it's just the loop, no vocals. I set a cue point right at the top of that stretch on every record I carry. Call it the break cue. When I'm mixing out of amapiano or club and the incoming rap record needs to sit for a while, I jump to the break cue, let the loop ride under the outgoing record for 16 bars, and the room hears drums, not a verse fighting a verse. It takes 20 seconds a record during prep. What's your prep routine?
caption: Midweek prep tip. Every 90s rap record has a stretch where it's just the loop and no vocals. I put a cue point at the top of it on every track I carry, the break cue, so when I'm coming out of amapiano or jersey club I can ride 16 bars of drums instead of a verse fighting a verse. 20 seconds per record in prep, hours of clean blends. What's your prep routine?
